topology_reference_used: none - no reference/topologies/*.md matches an MCU minimum system (only buck.md exists); researched from primary ST sources

decisions.what: VDD(16)/VSS(15) decoupling: 1x 100 nF ceramic across the pin pair, plus a share of a ~4.7 uF bulk cap on the VDD net. REQUIRED.
decisions.why: Datasheet Figure 12 'Power supply scheme' shows every VDD/VSS pair decoupled with filtering ceramics and its caption states caps 'must be decoupled ... as shown above'. The figure's '2x100nF + 1x4.7uF' set is drawn for the family's largest package (2 VDD/2 VSS pin pairs); TSSOP-20 has exactly ONE VDD pin (16) and ONE VSS pin (15) per Table 11 / Figure 8, so the per-pin-pair set (1x100nF, sharing the one 4.7uF bulk cap the net needs) applies once. AN4325's own BOM (Table 4, 'Mandatory components') independently specifies 100 nF (C1/C2) + 4.7 uF (C6) for the VDD/VSS net.
decisions.source: STM32F030x4/x6/x8/xC datasheet, ST DocID024849 Rev 3: section 6.1.6 Figure 12 + caption (p.41/91); Table 11 pin definitions, VDD/VSS TSSOP20 column (p.27-31/91); Figure 8 TSSOP20 pinout (p.26/91). AN4325 'Getting started with STM32F030xx hardware development', ST DocID024966 Rev 1, Table 4 'Mandatory components' (p.23/27).

decisions.what: VDDA(5) decoupling: 10 nF + 1 uF ceramic, returned to the VSS net (TSSOP-20 has no separate VSSA pin). REQUIRED.
decisions.why: Same Figure 12 scheme, VDDA/VSSA branch, same 'must be decoupled ... as shown' caption. AN4325 Table 4 independently confirms C3=10nF + C5=1uF 'Used for VDDA'. Table 11 lists VSSA as '-' (not bonded) on the TSSOP20/LQFP32 columns, so on this exact package the analog decoupling return has no dedicated VSSA pin to go to and must share the VSS/digital-ground net - a package fact, not a design gap.
decisions.source: Datasheet DocID024849 Rev 3, Figure 12 (p.41/91); Table 11 VDDA row ('13 9 5 5') and VSSA row ('12 8 - -') (p.27-31/91). AN4325 DocID024966 Rev 1, Table 4 (p.23/27).

decisions.what: VDDA tied directly to VDD with a plain trace (single supply). The connection itself is REQUIRED. An external filtering circuit on that connection is RECOMMENDED only, not required - excluded by this board's mode. VDDA-must-be->=VDD / VDDA-must-arrive-first sequencing is satisfied trivially because VDDA and VDD are the same net (zero possible delta, simultaneous arrival).
decisions.why: Datasheet section 3.5.1: 'VDDA = from VDD to 3.6 V ... The VDDA voltage level must be always greater or equal to the VDD voltage level and must be provided first.' AN4325 section 1.1: 'When a single supply is used, VDDA must be externally connected to VDD. It is recommended to use an external filtering circuit in order to ensure a noise free VDDA.' - required-vs-recommended split is explicit in ST's own wording. Confirmed by ST's own reference schematic (AN4325 Figure 9): VDDA is wired to VDD with a bare trace, no filter component. The Schottky-diode option mentioned in the same AN4325 paragraph applies only to the different case 'When VDDA is different from VDD' - not this board's topology.
decisions.source: Datasheet DocID024849 Rev 3, section 3.5.1 (p.13/91). AN4325 DocID024966 Rev 1, section 1.1 (p.6/27) and Figure 9 reference schematic (p.24/27).

decisions.what: NRST(4): permanent internal pull-up, typ 40 kOhm (25-55 kOhm range) - no external pull-up needed. An external ~0.1 uF NRST capacitor is shown only as part of an 'External reset circuit' example and is RECOMMENDED, not required - excluded by this board's mode (also: its own stated purpose in AN4325's BOM is debouncing a reset BUTTON, which this board does not have).
decisions.why: Datasheet: 'The NRST pin input driver uses the CMOS technology. It is connected to a permanent pull-up resistor, RPU' (always on, not switchable) - directly answers 'is an external pull-up needed' = no. Table 49 gives RPU = 25/40/55 kOhm min/typ/max. Figure 21 'Recommended NRST pin protection' draws the 0.1 uF cap inside a dashed circle explicitly labelled 'External reset circuit', footnoted 'The external capacitor protects the device against parasitic resets' - protective framing, not a stated requirement for the device to run or be debugged. AN4325's own component table ties the equivalent cap (C4, 100 nF) explicitly to 'Ceramic capacitor for RESET button' - this board has no reset button (excluded by mode), which independently removes the cap's stated use case.
decisions.source: Datasheet DocID024849 Rev 3, section 6.3.15 'NRST pin characteristics', Table 49 (p.65/91), Figure 21 + footnotes (p.66/91). AN4325 DocID024966 Rev 1, Table 5 'Optional components', row C4 (p.23/27). Cross-checked independently by the sibling research/interface-swd.md (same board), which reaches the same required-vs-recommended conclusion from the same primary citations.

decisions.what: BOOT0(1): LOW selects boot from main Flash (the only mode this board wants); the pin has NO documented internal pull, unlike NRST.
decisions.why: Boot mode table (BOOT0=0, nBOOT1=x) -> 'Main Flash memory is selected as boot area' - cross-checked in two independent ST documents with identical content. Table 11's pin-type legend defines I/O structure 'B' as simply 'Dedicated BOOT0 pin', with no pull-up/down language - contrast directly against the SAME legend's 'RST' entry, 'Bidirectional reset pin with embedded weak pull-up resistor'. The presence of pull wording for RST and its total absence for BOOT0, in the same legend, is the datasheet's own basis for treating BOOT0 as having no internal pull. A pin sampled by hardware before any software runs, with no internal pull and left unconnected, has an undefined logic level at the moment boot mode is latched (4th SYSCLK rising edge after reset) - a distinct, more acute issue than the general 'floating GPIO wastes power' guidance that applies to ordinary software-configurable I/O (see the unused-pins decision below), because BOOT0 cannot be configured by software before it is sampled.
decisions.source: AN4325 DocID024966 Rev 1, Table 2 'Boot modes' (p.17/27), cross-checked against RM0360 DocID025023 Rev 4, section 2.5 'Boot configuration' Table 3 (identical table, independent document). Datasheet DocID024849 Rev 3, Table 11 pin-type legend (p.30-31/91) and Figure 8 TSSOP20 pinout, pin 1 = BOOT0 (p.26/91).

decisions.what: BOOT0 resistor: 10 kOhm pull-down from BOOT0 to GND (this board's own topology - no switch, no jumper). REQUIRED support per this board's own scope rule, since the pin has no internal pull and must be held LOW for repeatable boot-from-flash.
decisions.why: AN4325's reference design uses R2 = 10 kOhm on the BOOT0 net, explicitly captioned 'Used for BOOT0 pin' with the caveat 'This value is given only as a typical example' - i.e. ST does not claim precision, just a safe, small, conventional value (this board takes the value, not the switch topology AN4325 draws around it: AN4325's R2 sits between a user-selectable SW1 switch and BOOT0, letting a dev board pick system-bootloader mode; this board only ever wants flash-boot, so the switch is dropped as an excluded config strap and R2 becomes a plain pull-down to GND).
decisions.source: AN4325 DocID024966 Rev 1, Table 5 'Optional components', row R2, and Figure 9 schematic 'Boot mode' block (p.23-24/27). Requirements.md section 2 point 5 (this board's own scope rule making a datasheet-required boot-mode resistor in-scope, not an excluded config strap).

decisions.what: SWD (PA13=SWDIO pin 19, PA14=SWCLK pin 20): come up as dedicated SWD pins immediately after reset, no software action needed. SWDIO has an internal pull-up active at reset; SWCLK has an internal pull-down active at reset, both 25/40/55 kOhm (min/typ/max) - same weak-pull spec block as any GPIO. No external series or bias resistors are needed or recommended.
decisions.why: Datasheet Table 11 footnote 7: 'After reset, these pins are configured as SWDIO and SWCLK alternate functions, and the internal pull-up on SWDIO pin and internal pull-down on SWCLK pin are activated.' AN4325 section 4.3.3: 'Having embedded pull-up and pull-down resistors removes the need to add external resistors.' Pull magnitude sourced from Table 46 'I/O static characteristics' (the generic weak pull-up/pull-down spec every AF pin uses; no separate table exists for the debug pins). Cross-checked pin assignment two ways: the datasheet's own Figure 8 pinout image and AN4325's Table 3 'SWD port pins' both independently show SWDIO=PA13, SWCLK=PA14.
decisions.source: Datasheet DocID024849 Rev 3, Table 11 footnote 7 (p.31-32/91), Table 46 (p.60-61/91), Figure 8 (p.26/91). AN4325 DocID024966 Rev 1, sections 4.2-4.3.4 (p.18-19/27), Table 3 (p.18/27).

decisions.what: SWD pins CAN be released to plain GPIO in software (not done on this board - J2 needs them as SWD permanently).
decisions.why: 'the MCU offers the possibility to disable the SWD, therefore releasing the associated pins for general-purpose I/O (GPIO) usage. For more details on how to disable SWD port, refer to the RM0360 section on I/O pin alternate function multiplexer and mapping.' Recorded for completeness per the assignment; this pipeline delivers hardware only (no firmware), so nothing in this board's design exercises this path, and the schematic must not route PA13/PA14 to J3 (the GPIO header) since that would create a pin conflict with J2.

decisions.what: Unused I/O tie-off (pull to a defined level, or drive as output) is a RECOMMENDED EMC/power-consumption practice, not a functional requirement. Floating digital inputs are described as a noise/current-consumption concern, never as a damage or non-function risk. Excluded by this board's mode (no added pull parts on unused pins, including PF0/PF1 when not used as OSC pins).
decisions.why: AN4325 section 5.6, verbatim: 'To increase EMC performance and avoid extra power consumption, unused clocks, counters or I/Os, should not be left free.' The datasheet's own general I/O current-consumption discussion uses the same framing: 'Any floating input pin can also settle to an intermediate voltage level or switch inadvertently, as a result of external electromagnetic noise. To avoid current consumption related to floating pins, they must either be configured in analog mode, or forced internally to a definite digital value.' Both sources motivate the practice by efficiency/EMC, not correctness - this is the required-vs-recommended line this board's scope tier draws. NOTE: this general guidance covers ordinary software-configurable GPIOs and does not apply to BOOT0, which is hardware-sampled before software runs (see the BOOT0 decisions above, kept separate deliberately).
decisions.source: AN4325 DocID024966 Rev 1, section 5.6 'Unused I/Os and features' (p.21/27). Datasheet DocID024849 Rev 3, I/O current-consumption discussion (p.47-48/91 area).

decisions.what: Oscillator: HSI (internal 8 MHz RC) is the default CPU clock selected automatically at reset. The part runs with zero external clock components. SWD debug access does not depend on which system clock is selected. When unused, OSC_IN/OSC_OUT (PF0=pin2, PF1=pin3) default to ordinary floating-input GPIOs.
decisions.why: Datasheet section 3.6 'Clocks and startup': 'System clock selection is performed on startup, however the internal RC 8 MHz oscillator is selected as default CPU clock on reset.' AN4325 section 2.3 'HSI clock': 'The HSI RC oscillator has the advantage of providing a clock source at low cost (no external components).' SWD independence from the system clock is a reasoned conclusion (not a single ST quote): RM0360 describes SWD-DP as a '2-pin (clock and data) interface' clocked by SWCLK, which the debug probe drives externally; nothing in the datasheet, RM0360 or AN4325 conditions debug-port availability on HSE/HSI selection. Table 11's general note - 'Unless otherwise specified by a note, all I/Os are set as floating inputs during and after reset' - applies to PF0/PF1 with no override note attached; AN4325's HSE-bypass description independently confirms OSC_OUT reverts to plain GPIO whenever the oscillator block isn't consuming it ('the OSC_OUT pin can be used a GPIO'), reinforcing the same conclusion for the always-off (HSI-default) case this board uses.
decisions.source: Datasheet DocID024849 Rev 3, section 3.6 (p.13-14/91), Table 11 general note and PF0/PF1 rows (p.27/91), Figure 8 (p.26/91). AN4325 DocID024966 Rev 1, section 2.3 (p.14/27), section 2.1 HSE-bypass paragraph (p.14/27). RM0360 DocID025023 Rev 4, SWD-DP description.

layout_notes: Decoupling caps 'must be placed as close as possible to, or below, the appropriate pins on the underside of the PCB' - datasheet Figure 12 caution note, DocID024849 Rev 3 p.41/91.
AN4325 Figure 8 'Typical layout for VDD/VSS pair' shows a via to the VDD plane and a via to the VSS plane straddling the decoupling cap, tight to the pin - DocID024966 Rev 1 section 5.4, p.20-21/27.

TSSOP-20 has no separate VSSA pin (Table 11 shows '-' for VSSA on this package/LQFP32) - VDDA's local decoupling necessarily returns to the shared VSS/GND pour on this exact part/package, not a separate analog ground plane. A package fact to hand to P6/P7, not a defect to fix.

AN4325 section 5.3 (general EMC guidance, not this-part-specific): separate VDD/VDDA supply routing, single-point ground return, minimized supply-loop area recommended for analog performance - informational since this board's VDDA is tied straight to VDD per the required decision above.

AN4325 sections 5.1/5.2: a multilayer board with dedicated GND and VDD layers is preferred 'for technical reasons' (decoupling + shielding) but explicitly acknowledged as not always economical - informational; this board's own layer count is earned by the layout per requirements.md section 5, not fixed by this note.

On the TSSOP20 package, SWDIO(19)/SWCLK(20) sit adjacent at one corner with VSS(15)/VDD(16) on the same side, while NRST is pin 4 on the opposite side (datasheet Figure 8) - J2 cannot take all its MCU-side signals off one package edge. Flagged for P6 placement; not this research's decision to make.

errata.item: No errata items found affecting NRST, BOOT0, VDDA, or SWD/debug for this device family in the revision reviewed.
errata.source: STM32F030x4/x6/x8/xC errata sheet, ST DocID025065 Rev 3, October 2016 - full contents list (System, USART, GPIO, I2C, SPI, RTC, ADC, IWDG) read; none of the 16 listed items touch these nets.

errata.item: GPIO erratum 2.3.1 exists ('Extra consumption on GPIOs PC0..5 on 48-pin and PB0 on 20-pin devices') and names STM32F030F4 specifically, but is hardware-irrelevant to this board: it only triggers if software reconfigures PB0 to analog mode, and PB0 is not bonded to any external pin on the TSSOP-20 package (confirmed against the datasheet's own Table 11 / Figure 8 - no PB0 anywhere in the 20-pin list; the pin exists only at the silicon level for this package). This pipeline also delivers no firmware. Recorded and dismissed rather than silently dropped.

Revision-currency caveat: st.com was unreachable from this research environment (both direct curl and WebFetch time out identically, consistent with a network-level block rather than a bot-detection page - confirmed against a working control fetch to example.com and to the LCSC mirror). All four ST documents used here (datasheet, RM0360, AN4325, errata) were obtained from credible third-party mirrors of the same primary ST PDFs, but each is 1-3 revisions behind the current st.com-hosted version (errata specifically: Rev 3 Oct-2016 read vs. current ES0219 Rev 6 Mar-2024 per web search - the largest gap of the four, and the document type most likely to have gained new entries since). Core electrical/pin facts used above (pinout, boot table, decoupling scheme, NRST/BOOT0/SWD pull behavior) are extremely unlikely to change across a mature, unchanged-silicon part's revisions, but a newer errata revision was not directly checked.
